name: Gustave Courbet
findings: Uses dark olive brown 1.4x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 1513 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, lagoon blue turns up as a small accent in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 7.8x the archive's rate (from 1513 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, dusty rose brown turns up as the lightest note in 71% of the paintings that hold it, 3.0x the archive's rate (from 1513 paintings here).
Pairs buff orange with ochre yellow more than chance would predict (3 of 1513 paintings here).
Pairs light blue grey with manatee more than chance would predict (3 of 1513 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (smoky black, dark jungle green, dark olive brown) covers 68% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from smoky black, dark jungle green to smoky black, dark olive brown.
Paints most like Yamamoto Hōsui among the painters in this archive, by palette.
